scope: Forty-five close-only synthetic direct/stock relayd HTTP/TCP body/parser observations; separate unchanged 163 ordinary leaves. Native execution of host cross-build; bounded research under #16.

compatibility_assessment.tcp: Candidate to prefer for further transport research: retains complete-input direct outcomes in this corpus and avoids a second HTTP parser, but truncated-body response differs; no adoption approval.
compatibility_assessment.http: Valid benign/attack/size/media outcomes preserved here, but bad chunk, conflicting lengths, truncated body and unsupported coding differ. Conflict control reached the client deadline without response; this does not qualify bounded appliance rejection.
compatibility_assessment.both: Identical CL and CL+TE controls accepted and normalized to the same inspection view; exact benign body digests agree. No anti-smuggling or full parser safety claim.

limitations: No response before the client deadline is a retained observed timeout, not successful bounded appliance rejection. EOF/other errors do not establish a particular relayd internal mechanism.

Source reads are application consumption; connection reads include headers/prefetch/drain and are observational. Cleanup flags cover owned accepted inspection connections (which may be absent on ingress rejection), server joins/listener absence and foreground daemon/socket/VM teardown.
Health polling deliberately excluded; no claim that this fixes earlier pipeline/health/generation failures.
Fresh close-only synthetic peers do not qualify persistent/pipelined/concurrent traffic, TLS/Host/SNI, trusted sender or general parser compatibility.
Current comparison binary is host cross-built; earlier native source builds and connected receipts retain original scope.
Full CRS/OWASP coverage, real workload false positives, image/installed daemon lineage, architecture selection and appliance adoption remain open.
